# Raptor Studio MCP server

Raptor Studio ships a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server, so an AI assistant can
build, validate, simulate and explain reliability block diagrams. It exposes **66 tools**, a set of
**resources** and three **prompts**. The numbers come from the same engine as the desktop app and the
`raptor` command line.

The server is named `raptor-studio`. Its entry points are `raptor-studio-mcp`, `raptor mcp` and
`python -m raptor.mcp`. The tutorial's last chapter ("RAPTOR from an AI Assistant") has worked examples;
this page is the reference.

## Install

```bash
pip install "raptor-studio[mcp]"
```

Or run it without installing anything: `uvx raptor-studio-mcp --workspace ~/raptor-models` (the
`raptor-studio-mcp` package pins the matching `raptor-studio[mcp]`). From a checkout: `uv sync --extra mcp`. Python 3.12 or newer. `render_diagram` needs Qt's system libraries (use
`--no-render` on a headless machine without them).

## Connect a client

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude mcp add raptor-studio -- raptor-studio-mcp --workspace ~/raptor-models
```

**Claude Desktop** (`claude_desktop_config.json`), and most other clients that take a JSON config:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "raptor-studio": {
      "command": "raptor-studio-mcp",
      "args": ["--workspace", "/home/you/raptor-models"]
    }
  }
}
```

If the command is not on `PATH`, give the full path to the virtual environment's `raptor-studio-mcp`. From a
checkout use `"command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--directory", "/path/to/repo", "python", "-m", "raptor.mcp"]`.

**OpenCode** (`opencode.json`; OpenCode reloads it when saved):

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "raptor-studio": {
        "type": "local",
        "command": ["raptor-studio-mcp", "--workspace", "/home/you/raptor-models"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

From a checkout, use
`"command": ["uv", "run", "--directory", "/path/to/repo", "python", "-m", "raptor.mcp"]`. The CLI writes the
same entry: `opencode mcp add raptor-studio -- raptor-studio-mcp --workspace ~/raptor-models`.

To try the tools by hand: `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector raptor-studio-mcp --workspace ~/raptor-models`
opens the MCP Inspector (it needs Node.js).

## Transports

| Transport | Use | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stdio` (default) | The client launches the server as a child process. | Listens on no network port. |
| `http` (Streamable HTTP) | A server shared by several clients, or run in a container. | Default `127.0.0.1:8765/mcp`. |

```bash
raptor-studio-mcp --transport http --port 8765 --token-file ~/.raptor-token
```

HTTP safety rules: **a bearer token is required** (`--token-file` or `--token-env`, at least 16 characters, for example
`head -c 32 /dev/urandom | base64 > ~/.raptor-token; chmod 600 ~/.raptor-token`); the server refuses to start without
one unless `--allow-unauthenticated` is given, which is for single-user machines only because any local process can
then reach the workspace, and which never applies to a non-loopback `--host`. Every request needs
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`; a client address that sends ten wrong tokens in a minute is locked out for a minute
(HTTP 429). Browser cross-origin calls are blocked unless `--allow-origin` lists the origin; the Host header is
checked against DNS rebinding; `--tls-cert`/`--tls-key` serve HTTPS, and a non-loopback bind refuses plaintext HTTP
unless `--allow-insecure-http` is given explicitly. Request bodies are capped, and at most two long jobs
(`simulate`, `sweep_parameter`, `compare_models` and `start_run`) run at once; at most four `start_run` jobs may be
queued or running, and a fifth is refused with `limit_exceeded`. `--port 0` picks a free port and prints the URL as
the first line of output.

All clients of one server share one workspace, so give each person or project their own server (and token).

## Options

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--workspace DIR` | `~/.local/share/raptor-studio/mcp` | Where models, runs and renders live. |
| `--transport {stdio,http}` | `stdio` | See above. |
| `--host`, `-p/--port`, `--path` | `127.0.0.1`, `8765`, `/mcp` | http bind address, port and endpoint path. |
| `--token-file FILE`, `--token-env VAR` | none | http bearer token, at least 16 characters (one or the other). Required unless `--allow-unauthenticated`. |
| `--allow-unauthenticated` | off | http: serve loopback with no token (single-user machines only). |
| `--allow-origin ORIGIN` | none | http: allowed browser Origin; repeatable. |
| `--tls-cert FILE`, `--tls-key FILE` | none | http: serve HTTPS. |
| `--allow-insecure-http` | off | http: permit plaintext bearer tokens on a non-loopback bind (not recommended). |
| `--read-only` | off | Refuse every tool that creates, edits or deletes a model or exports a file. Opening, analysing and simulating stay allowed. |
| `--no-render` | off | Do not expose `render_diagram`. |
| `--allow-write DIR` | none | Extra directory `save_model_as` may write to; repeatable. |
| `--allow-read DIR` | none | Extra directory `open_model` may read model files from; repeatable. The workspace and examples are always readable. |
| `--retain-days N` | 30 | Days to keep run and render artefacts. Models are kept. |
| `--max-runs N` | 5000 | Hard cap on `num_runs` per call. |
| `--log-level LEVEL` | `INFO` | `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `WARNING`, `ERROR`. |

Nothing outside the workspace is written unless `--allow-write` permits it, and `open_model` only reads the
workspace, bundled examples and `--allow-read` directories. Unknown tool parameters are rejected, not ignored, so
a misspelt `num_runs` fails loudly instead of running with the default.

## Tools

A trailing `?` marks an optional parameter. "read-only" tools change nothing. "writes" tools edit a model or
write run results to the workspace; "destructive" tools delete or undo. `--read-only` refuses the tools that
edit or delete models or export files, while opening, analysing and simulating stay allowed. Each tool's full
description and input/output schema is what the server sends on `tools/list`.

| Tool | Kind | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `add_annotation` | writes | Add a drawing annotation (text box, rect, ellipse or arrow). | `model_id`, `kind`?, `text`?, `adjacent_to`?, `side`?, `gap`?, `x`?, `y`?, `w`?, `h`?, `from_`?, `to`?, `x1`?, `y1`?, `x2`?, `y2`?, `parent`?, `style`? |
| `add_block` | writes | Add a block to the model. | `model_id`, `name`, `fail_dist`?, `fail_params`?, `repair_dist`?, `repair_params`?, `parent`?, `after`? |
| `add_elements` | writes | Add many blocks, nodes or events with one save. | `model_id`, `elements` |
| `add_event` | writes | Add an event to the model.  `prob` is its probability (0-1). | `model_id`, `name`, `prob`? |
| `add_hierarchy` | writes | Create an empty hierarchy -- a sub-model boundary -- with its In and Out markers already wired up correctly. | `model_id`, `name`, `parent`? |
| `add_node` | writes | Add a node to the model. | `model_id`, `type`?, `k`?, `name`?, `parent`? |
| `auto_layout` | writes | Re-arrange a model's diagram onto the shared layered grid. | `model_id`, `hierarchy`?, `selectors`? |
| `build_model` | writes | Build a complete model from a friendly .rbds spec document. | `name`, `spec`?, `auto_layout`?, `validate_model`?, `model_id`?, `spec_path`? |
| `cancel_run` | writes | Ask a background job to stop (checked between replications, and while a large model is still being set up). | `job_id` |
| `close_model` | destructive | Close one or more models.  Set delete=true to also remove their files. | `model_id`, `delete`? |
| `collapse_selection` | writes | Move existing blocks/nodes/events into a new hierarchy, rewiring the boundary. | `model_id`, `selectors`, `name`?, `parent`? |
| `compare_models` | writes | Compare 2–5 models or runs side by side. | `models`, `num_runs`?, `metrics`? |
| `configure_block_defaults` | writes | Set the distributions `add_block` uses when you don't name any. | `action`?, `fail_dist`?, `fail_params`?, `repair_dist`?, `repair_params`? |
| `configure_maintenance` | writes | Configure preventive maintenance for a block. | `model_id`, `selector`, `pm_freq`?, `pm_duration_dist`?, `pm_params`?, `trigger_name`?, `defer_flags`? |
| `configure_phases` | writes | Configure mission phases. | `model_id`, `phases`?, `assignments`?, `mode`?, `remove`?, `unassign`? |
| `configure_sparing` | writes | Configure sparing for a block. | `model_id`, `selector`, `mode`?, `spare_pool`?, `stock`?, `restock_every`?, `emergency`?, `slo`?, `level`?, `quantity`?, `slo_time`? |
| `configure_system` | writes | Configure system-level simulation settings. | `model_id`, `run_length`?, `num_runs`?, `termination`?, `start_stats`?, `units`?, `weak_link`?, `cost`?, `capacity`?, `gy_threshold`?, `yr_threshold`?, `system_streams`?, `display_unit`?, `flow_generated`? |
| `connect` | writes | Connect two elements with a link. | `model_id`, `from_element`?, `to_element`?, `replace`? |
| `connect_many` | writes | Create many links with one save. | `model_id`, `links` |
| `create_model` | writes | Create a new model. | `name`, `template`?, `n`?, `k`? |
| `delete_annotation` | destructive | Delete one annotation by id.  Returns {deleted, kind}. | `model_id`, `annotation_id` |
| `delete_element` | destructive | Delete an element from the model. | `model_id`, `selector`, `reconnect`? |
| `delete_elements` | destructive | Delete many elements with one save. | `model_id`, `selectors`, `reconnect`? |
| `delete_file` | destructive | Delete a file previously exported with `save_model_as` (or any other file inside the workspace or an --allow-write directory). | `path` |
| `delete_link` | destructive | Delete one link by id, leaving both elements in place. | `model_id`, `link_id` |
| `describe_metrics` | read-only | List the result metrics, and optionally show one run's values. | `run_id`?, `model_id`? |
| `describe_model` | read-only | Describe the model structure. | `model_id`, `detail`?, `level`? |
| `diff_models` | read-only | Say what is different between two models (their inputs, not their results). | `model_a`, `model_b`, `ignore`?, `match`?, `detail`? |
| `estimate_runtime` | read-only | Estimate wall-clock time for a simulation before running it. | `model_id`, `num_runs`?, `run_length`?, `workers`?, `importance`? |
| `export_tables` | writes | Write tables to files: CSV, text, or one spreadsheet. | `model_id`, `run_id`?, `tables`?, `formats`?, `folder`? |
| `extract_hierarchy` | writes | Build a standalone model from one hierarchy (a port extension), or just list what crosses its boundary. | `model_id`, `hierarchy`, `treatments`?, `report_only`?, `name`? |
| `failure_effects` | read-only | Run failure-effects analysis (Raptor workbook Chapter 10). | `model_id`, `fail`?, `repair`?, `phase`? |
| `failure_effects_batch` | read-only | Run many failure-effects scenarios in one call, on one model set-up. | `model_id`, `scenarios`, `include_log`? |
| `get_element` | read-only | Read one block, node, event, hierarchy or link back in full. | `model_id`, `selector`, `detail`? |
| `get_report` | read-only | Get a paginated report section from a completed run. | `run_id`, `section`?, `run_number`?, `format`?, `offset`?, `limit`? |
| `get_run_results` | read-only | One completed run as a single assessable bundle. | `run_id`, `top`? |
| `get_table` | read-only | Read one table: its column headers and a page of rows. | `model_id`, `table`, `run_id`?, `offset`?, `limit`? |
| `get_timeseries` | read-only | Get time-series data from a completed run, for the client to plot. | `run_id`, `series`?, `runs`?, `points`? |
| `list_annotations` | read-only | List a model's diagram annotations. | `model_id`, `parent`? |
| `list_distributions` | read-only | List every distribution supported by the RAPTOR engine. | — |
| `list_models` | read-only | List open models and (optionally) bundled example models. | `include_examples`?, `limit`?, `offset`? |
| `list_tables` | read-only | List the tables that can be read or exported. | `model_id`, `run_id`? |
| `manage_rates` | writes | Manage the model's named Rates library. | `model_id`, `action`?, `name`?, `expr`?, `description`? |
| `manage_resources` | writes | Create, list, edit or delete a resource pool (shared crew/equipment). | `model_id`, `action`?, `name`?, `num_in`?, `spare_cost`?, `fixed_per_use`?, `per_time_unit`?, `phases`? |
| `manage_spare_pools` | writes | Create, list, edit or delete a spare pool. | `model_id`, `action`?, `name`?, `stock`?, `new_spares`?, `arrive_every`?, `eso`?, `emer_time`?, `slo`?, `level`?, `quantity`?, `slo_time`?, `rso`?, `spare_cost`?, `emer_ship_cost`? |
| `manage_triggers` | writes | Create, list, edit or delete a trigger (for triggered PM). | `model_id`, `action`?, `name`?, `init_used`?, `dist`?, `params`?, `repeats`? |
| `move_element` | writes | Move a block, node, event or hierarchy to another hierarchy level. | `model_id`, `selector`, `parent` |
| `open_model` | writes | Copy a model file into the workspace and return its handle. | `path` |
| `ping` | read-only | Health-check: returns 'pong' if the server is running. | — |
| `read_doc` | read-only | Read a documentation source as text (paginated). | `name`, `offset`?, `limit`? |
| `redo_last_edit` | destructive | Step one edit forward again after `undo_last_edit` (multi-step). | `model_id` |
| `render_diagram` | read-only | Render the model diagram as a PNG image. | `model_id`, `level`?, `zoom_to`?, `margin`?, `highlight`?, `theme`?, `max_px`?, `include_annotations`? |
| `render_diagram_svg` | read-only | Draw one level of the diagram as SVG text, without Qt. | `model_id`, `level`?, `zoom_to`?, `margin`?, `highlight`?, `theme`?, `include_annotations`? |
| `run_status` | read-only | Progress of a job started with `start_run`. | `job_id` |
| `save_model_as` | destructive | Save a model to a file path. | `model_id`, `path`, `format`? |
| `search_docs` | read-only | Search the RAPTOR tutorial docs for passages matching a query. | `query`, `limit`? |
| `simulate` | writes | Run a simulation and return structured results. | `model_id`, `num_runs`?, `run_length`?, `collect_events`?, `workers`?, `date`?, `timeout_s`?, `confirm_long_run`?, `seed`?, `hierarchy`?, `treatments`?, `importance`? |
| `single_point_failures` | read-only | Find single-point failures in the model. | `model_id`, `workers`?, `limit`?, `offset`? |
| `start_run` | writes | Start a simulation in the background and return a job id immediately. | `model_id`, `num_runs`?, `run_length`?, `workers`?, `timeout_s`?, `collect_events`?, `seed`? |
| `sweep_parameter` | writes | Sweep a parameter across values and measure the impact. | `model_id`, `selector`, `field`, `values`, `num_runs`?, `metrics`? |
| `undo_last_edit` | destructive | Step one edit back (multi-step: call again to go further back). | `model_id` |
| `update_annotation` | writes | Patch one annotation. | `model_id`, `annotation_id`, `patch` |
| `update_element` | writes | Update fields on an element. | `model_id`, `selector`, `patch`, `full`? |
| `update_elements` | writes | Update many elements with one save. | `model_id`, `updates` |
| `validate_model` | read-only | Validate a model for structural and parameter errors. | `model_id` |
| `workspace_info` | read-only | Return the server workspace root and read/write rules. | — |

Typical flow: `open_model` or `build_model` → `validate_model` → `estimate_runtime` → `simulate` → `get_report`.
Use `get_element` to read one block back in full, and `read_doc('dependency')` before modelling a backup that
follows another unit: a dependent backup sits idle exactly when the unit it follows is down.

## Large models

A model with hundreds of blocks can spend minutes in set-up before its first replication, and a batch can run for
hours. What helps:

- **Run in the background.** `start_run` returns a job id at once; poll `run_status`. Its `phase` is `setting_up`
  while the model is prepared (with `setup`: `stage`, `done`, `total`, `percent`), then `simulating`, so a quiet
  start is not a hang. `cancel_run` stops a job between replications, or during set-up.
- **Cores.** Leave `workers` out and a model of 500+ blocks, events and nodes run 20+ times uses several cores
  (half the machine's, at most 8, never fewer than two). `simulate` and `start_run` report the `workers` used and
  `workers_auto`. Pass `workers=1` for the sequential numbers: a multi-core batch is repeatable but not
  bit-identical to a sequential one. This default is the server's only; the desktop app and `raptor run` keep theirs.
- **Big inputs by file.** `build_model` takes `spec_path`, a JSON file inside the workspace (or an `--allow-read`
  directory), instead of an inline `spec`. `open_model` already takes a workspace path to a `.rbds` or `.rbd`.
- **Many what-ifs in one call.** `failure_effects_batch` runs up to 2000 `{fail, repair, phase}` scenarios on one
  model set-up, each from the all-good state, and reports a scenario it cannot apply without stopping the rest.

## Resources

| URI | Type | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `raptor://examples` | application/json | List bundled example models as JSON. |
| `raptor://models` | application/json | Index of the open models (model_id, name, counts) as JSON. |
| `raptor://runs` | application/json | Index of completed runs kept in the workspace (newest first). |
| `raptor://examples/{name}` | text/plain | Read a bundled example model as .rbds text. |
| `raptor://models/{model_id}` | text/plain | Read the live model as .rbds text. |
| `raptor://runs/{run_id}/{section}` | text/plain | Read a full report section for a completed run. |
| `raptor://docs/{chapter}` | text/plain | Read a chapter of the tutorial book (new_docs/chapters/*.adoc). |
| `raptor://renders/{name}` | image/png | Read a rendered diagram PNG by file name. |

## Prompts

| Prompt | What it does | Arguments |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `new_availability_study` | Start a new availability study from a plain-English description. | `system_description`, `mission_hours` |
| `explain_model` | Explain an existing model in plain English. | `model_id` |
| `improve_availability` | Propose and test changes that improve availability. | `model_id`, `target` |

## Reporting problems

Open an issue at <https://github.com/openpowershift/RaptorStudio/issues> with the client, the tool call and the
server's `--log-level DEBUG` output. The tool list is a tested contract, so a change to it is
deliberate and shows in the diff of this page.
